li: Nam Co
Large saltwater lake on the Tibetan plateau, a sacred lake for Tibetans.
Siling Co
One of the largest lakes in Tibet.
Mansarovar (Mapam Yumco)
Sacred freshwater lake in Tibet near Mount Kailash, at about 4,590 m. The Sutlej and Brahmaputra both rise in this region.
Yamdrok Lake
One of the four holy lakes of Tibet.
Pangong Tso
High-altitude saltwater lake in Ladakh, shared with Tibet. Its water is brackish yet it freezes in winter.
Krishna Raja Sagar
Reservoir on the Kaveri near Mysuru, Karnataka.
Bhadra Reservoir
Reservoir on the Bhadra river (Tungabhadra system) in Karnataka.
Tungabhadra Reservoir
Reservoir behind the Tungabhadra Dam at Hosapete, Karnataka.
Tarbela Reservoir
Pakistan’s largest reservoir, on the Indus.
Gobind Sagar
Reservoir of the Bhakra Dam on the Sutlej in Himachal Pradesh.
Hirakud Reservoir
Man-made lake on the Mahanadi in Odisha, one of the longest earthen dams in the world.
Nagarjuna Sagar
Large reservoir on the Krishna on the Telangana–Andhra Pradesh border.
Kaptai Lake
Largest man-made lake in Bangladesh, on the Karnaphuli river.
Gandhi Sagar
Reservoir on the Chambal in Madhya Pradesh.
MK: Asia’s largest brackish-water lagoon, on the Odisha coast.
Famous lake in Srinagar, Kashmir, known for houseboats.
One of Asia’s largest freshwater lakes, fed by the Jhelum in Kashmir.
India’s largest inland salt lake, in Rajasthan.
Largest freshwater lake in the northeast, in Manipur, with floating islands (phumdis).
Longest lake in India, a backwater system in Kerala.
Second-largest brackish lagoon in India, on the Andhra Pradesh–Tamil Nadu coast.

R.info: Enters India at Shipki La and feeds the Bhakra Nangal dam. It is the longest of the five rivers of Punjab.
Passes Delhi and Agra and is the Ganga’s longest tributary. The Taj Mahal stands on its bank.
India’s most sacred river and the lifeline of the northern plains. Haridwar, Prayagraj, Varanasi and Patna lie on its banks.

R.mouth: Joins the Ganga delta, Bay of Bengal
R.info: Enters Arunachal Pradesh as the Siang and flows through Assam as a wide braided river with the world’s largest river island, Majuli.
Flows west in a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges. Famous for the Dhuandhar falls and the Sardar Sarovar dam.
The other major west-flowing river of the peninsula, running just south of the Narmada.
Its Hirakud Dam is one of the longest earthen dams in the world. Cuttack stands on its delta.
The longest peninsular river, often called Dakshin Ganga. It hosts the Kumbh Mela at Nashik.
Flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh and irrigates a vast rain-shadow region.
A rain-fed river that still flows well in the dry months thanks to both monsoons. Splits into islands at Srirangapatna and Srirangam.
One of the few rivers that cross the Tropic of Cancer twice. It flows through Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Gujarat.
